how_to_use: Has two contact groups, each with two legs (1.l/1.r are always tied together internally, and separately 2.l/2.r are always tied together — either leg of a group works identically, it's not a wiring choice). Pressing the button bridges the two groups together; releasing separates them. Wire one leg from each group: one group to a digital input (with a pull-down resistor to ground, or use INPUT_PULLUP and skip the resistor), the other group to 5V or GND depending on which style you're using.

plain.what: A button that connects its legs only while you press it.
plain.how: Put it across the middle gap of the breadboard. Wire one side to an Arduino pin and the other side to power; the Arduino can then tell when it's pressed.

pins.2: the other side (legs on the same side are always joined)
